html:
The Siege of Famagusta was the Ottoman siege of the last Venetian stronghold on Cyprus, from September 1570 to August 1571, which completed the Ottoman conquest of the island.

The Ottomans landed in 1570 and took Nicosia after a short siege, killing much of its population. Famagusta, under Marco Antonio Bragadin, held out for nearly a year. After it surrendered on terms, the Ottoman commander had Bragadin mutilated and flayed alive. The loss shocked Europe and helped bring about the Christian victory at Lepanto two months later, but Venice gave up Cyprus anyway. The Ottomans settled Turkish soldiers and peasants on the island, the origin of the Turkish Cypriot community, and restored the Orthodox church.
sum: The Siege of Famagusta was the Ottoman siege of the last Venetian stronghold on Cyprus, from September 1570 to August 1571, which completed the Ottoman conquest of the island.
